authority: Project working definition adopted by assistant under user delegation; not human annotation
target: Document relevance to concrete cyber threats and associated defense; separate from customer focus and claim truth

rules.R1: Positive requires an explicit cyber threat, concrete vulnerability, or defense tied to an identified threat or mechanism in the document body.
rules.R2: An explicit stolen-data, compromised-access or malicious-service claim is relevant even if not verified; relevance is not authenticity.
rules.R3: Tor, anonymity, cryptocurrency, price, product brand, security keywords or domain reputation alone never establish relevance.
rules.R4: Ordinary administration, accessibility, installation, privacy and finance instructions without a concrete cyber threat are negative.
rules.R5: A directory, mixed index, empty page or missing article is an abstention, never a negative example by default.
rules.R6: If ambiguous origin or missing context changes the relevance decision, abstain instead of inventing a compromise.
rules.R7: Navigation, testimonials, related links and repeated boilerplate do not independently establish the main document topic.
rules.R8: Evidence spans must match the immutable stored text. Negative labels also require full-text reading; one negative excerpt cannot prove absence of a threat.
rules.R9: Novelty and relevance are separate. Duplicate or unresolved-neighbor documents cannot enter the new training export.
rules.R10: Assistant annotations remain assistant annotations. Historical human labels are preserved until a separately traceable adjudication supersedes them.
